gloss: Draw your own theory of change
lede: The report ends by telling readers to draw their own theory of change. This page hands you the pen.

blocks.text: If you are thinking of starting something, we encourage you to draw your own TOC. Imagine the future, put the path to it into words, and draw the lines. It will surely be the first step in connecting you with someone else.
blocks.role: Theory of Change: Drawing a Map of Change, p.13

paragraphs: Z&C calls its theory of change "a navigation map to the future, showing what kind of society Z&C aims for and the route we will take to get there." The report's own tools are two: the {{term:logic-model}}, which runs from input and activity through output to short-, mid- and long-term outcomes, and the fifteen questions Z&C asks a company before investing. The tool below uses six of those questions, quoted as printed, and lays your answers out on the logic model's own frame.

blocks.heading: Draw your own map
blocks.intro: Six questions, one screen each. Your answers stay in this browser; nothing is sent anywhere. Come back and the draft will still be here.

ui.placeholder: Write as much or as little as you like.
ui.map_caption: Imagine the future, put the path to it into words, and draw the lines.
ui.fine: Stays on this device. Clearing your browser data clears it too.

questions.q: How does this business contribute to realizing a "thoughtful, healthy and enjoyable society"?
Whose awareness or behavior will this business influence or change, and in what ways?
What social impact does the business aim to achieve? How will it contribute to transforming society?
Does the growth of the business directly lead to an increase in social impact?
What will the funds be used for, and how will they be utilized?
What knowledge, experience, and networks do the founder and management team possess in relation to the business they are pursuing? What additional capacities will be required going forward?
